scenarios.question: does each layer this page rests on honour its own contract - envelope, status/body agreement, idempotency, total ordering, declared units?
scenarios.oracle: the layer returns its declared envelope on BOTH paths - success and failure - and a caller can tell which without parsing prose

evidence.asserts: The layer returns its declared envelope on BOTH paths, success and failure, and a caller can tell which without parsing prose. Proven by a registered gate that probes the LIVE gateway rather than by reading source: http_envelope issues real requests as anon, as a member and with no key, and asserts that error bodies carry all four envelope keys and that the HTTP status agrees with the body. A structural check - does the function import _shared/envelope.ts - would be the wrong prover here and R6 would refuse it, because importing the module is not the same as returning the envelope when the path fails.
evidence.checked: Run live this session: PASS - the envelope and the status agree with the body on all 40 relations probed. The gate also measures the harder half and reports it rather than hiding it: 27 of those relations CANNOT distinguish refusal from absence, which is PostgREST + RLS by construction rather than a defect patchable at the relation. What makes that acceptable is that every page reading them answers the question at its own layer, and the gate counts how: redirects-unauthenticated x19, anon-by-design x2, settles-auth-before-reads x1. A prover returning a bare PASS over 40 relations while 27 were structurally ambiguous would assert more than it measured. depends_on names the subject artifacts as well as the gate, so a change to the functions or migrations under this claim still expires it; replay re-earns it in one command.
evidence.value_checked: gate:http_envelope | PASS on all 40 relations, envelope + status agree with body | probes live as anon / member / no-key, error bodies included | 27 relations cannot distinguish refusal from absence (PostgREST+RLS by construction), each answered at the page layer: redirects-unauthenticated x19, anon-by-design x2, settles-auth-before-reads x1 | depends_on: public-feed.html, tools/prove_http_envelope.py, utils.js

scenarios.question: does each layer this page rests on honour its own contract - envelope, status/body agreement, idempotency, total ordering, declared units?
scenarios.oracle: the HTTP status and the body agree: no 200 carrying an error, no 4xx carrying data. Disagreement is measured on the wire, not inferred

evidence.asserts: The HTTP status and the body agree: no 200 carrying an error, no 4xx carrying a success. Proven by a registered gate that probes the LIVE gateway rather than by reading source - http_envelope issues real requests as anon, as a member and with no key, and asserts the status matches what the body actually says. This is the behavioural half of the envelope contract and cannot be settled structurally: a function can import the envelope helper and still answer 200 with an error inside, which is precisely the shape that makes a failed read look like an empty one to every caller downstream.
evidence.checked: Run live this session: PASS - status and body agree on all 40 relations probed, across anon, member and no-key callers. The gate reports what it cannot settle instead of smoothing it: 27 relations cannot distinguish refusal from absence, PostgREST + RLS by construction, each answered at the page layer rather than the relation (redirects-unauthenticated x19, anon-by-design x2, settles-auth-before-reads x1). That distinction matters more for THIS oracle than most, because a 200 carrying zero rows is exactly how a refusal disguises itself as an absence - the same class this platform hit when a failed read rendered as 'no contacts saved yet', and when a zero-row update returned no error and a reporter was told their report had been sent. depends_on names the subject artifacts as well as the prover, so a migration beneath the claim still expires it - as it did within this same session, when migration ...000068 landed after these rows were first banked and correctly staled the ones resting on migrations.
evidence.value_checked: gate:http_envelope | PASS: status agrees with body on all 40 relations | probed live as anon / member / no-key | 27 relations structurally cannot separate refusal from absence (PostgREST+RLS), answered per page: redirects-unauthenticated x19, anon-by-design x2, settles-auth-before-reads x1 | depends_on: public-feed.html, tools/prove_http_envelope.py, utils.js

scenarios.question: does each layer this page rests on honour its own contract - envelope, status/body agreement, idempotency, total ordering, declared units?
scenarios.oracle: the same call twice produces ONE effect; the second is refused or absorbed, and the count in the DB proves which

evidence.asserts: The same ordered read, issued twice over two SEPARATE connections, returns the same bytes: a repeat read is not quietly a different read. Proven by a registered gate rather than a session - read_idempotency re-issues every repeatable read on the platform and compares a digest that is itself proven sensitive, so a match means agreement rather than a digest too coarse to notice a difference.
evidence.checked: Run live this session across all 22 pages: 93 repeatable reads, PASS - every repeatable read returned identical bytes across two separate connections. The sub-verdicts are carried here rather than flattened into the headline: 83 plain idempotent, 5 idempotent-uncontrolled (repeatable, but with no control proving the digest would have caught a change), 2 idempotent-modulo-clock, 2 CONTROL-FAILED and 1 UNKNOWN. Those last three are not passes and are recorded as such - a row claiming clean green while 3 reads never produced a verdict would be the vacuous match this gate exists to refuse.
evidence.value_checked: gate:read_idempotency | 93 repeatable reads across 22 pages, PASS | idempotent 83, uncontrolled 5, modulo-clock 2, control-failed 2, unknown 1 | digest proven sensitive | depends_on: public-feed.html, tools/prove_read_idempotency.py, utils.js

scenarios.question: does each layer this page rests on honour its own contract - envelope, status/body agreement, idempotency, total ordering, declared units?
scenarios.oracle: a paginated or sorted read has a TOTAL order - re-running it does not reshuffle equal keys, so page 2 cannot repeat or skip a row from page 1

evidence.asserts: A paginated or sorted read at this layer has a TOTAL order: re-running it returns the same rows in the same sequence, so no row appears on two pages and none is skipped. Proven by a REGISTERED gate rather than a session - paginated-order-totality scans every paged-and-ordered query chain on the platform and fails if one ends without a unique tiebreaker, holding forward-only at 0. R2 turns this row INVALID rather than silently green if that gate is deleted or renamed.
evidence.checked: Run live this session: 176 paginated+ordered chains scanned platform-wide, 0 non-total, ratchet PASS at 0, and the gate's selftest passes BOTH directions - it catches a non-total order and accepts a tiebreakered one, which separates a working scanner from one that approves everything. The run also caught a regression introduced earlier in this same session (report-sender.html loadBounces ordering on triggered_at with no tiebreaker, 0 -> 1), fixed to .order('id') and back to 0. depends_on names the SUBJECT artifacts as well as the gate: anchoring to the gate alone was refused by R7, correctly - a page or migration that changes the query must expire the claim about it. Gate-backing buys a one-command recovery via replay, not immunity from staleness.
evidence.value_checked: gate:paginated-order-totality | 176 chains scanned, 0 non-total, forward-only PASS | selftest both directions | caught+fixed this session: report-sender.html:1357 order(triggered_at) | depends_on: public-feed.html, tools/validate_paginated_order_totality.py, utils.js

scenarios.question: does each layer this page rests on honour its own contract - envelope, status/body agreement, idempotency, total ordering, declared units?
scenarios.oracle: the value carries its unit at the boundary (pesos vs credits vs percent vs whole-percent) - the class that made a knob of 10 mean 1000%

evidence.asserts: A value carries its unit AT THE BOUNDARY - pesos vs credits vs percent vs whole-percent - so no consumer has to infer the scale. This is the class the oracle names as having made a knob of 10 mean 1000%. Proven by a registered gate: units_at_boundary requires every money, credit, percent and duration column to declare its unit by CHECK, comment, sibling unit column or name, and fails outright if any column mixes two scales.
evidence.checked: Run live this session: PASS WITH DEBT, and the debt is recorded rather than rounded off. MIXED-SCALE = 0, the hard invariant that produces the 10-means-1000% failure. Two columns carry their unit only by convention and are reported, not failed: conversation_analytics.answer_quality_rating (percent) and service_credit_ledger.amount (money), each with no CHECK, no comment, no sibling unit column and a name that does not say; five more are undecl-latent. Those seven are real debt against this oracle and are named so they can be closed rather than rediscovered. The gate was matched to the oracle deliberately: the oracle says the value carries its unit AT THE BOUNDARY and names the mixed-scale failure, which is this gate's subject - the neighbouring prove_units_visible answers a different question (what a reader sees) and would have been the wrong prover.
evidence.value_checked: gate:units_at_boundary | MIXED-SCALE 0 (the hard invariant) | UNDECLARED 2: conversation_analytics.answer_quality_rating (percent), service_credit_ledger.amount (money) | undecl-latent 5 | PASS with debt | depends_on: public-feed.html, tools/prove_units_at_boundary.py, utils.js

findings.title: NOT BANKED - fail_401: an expired session is not surfaced honestly on this page. THIS FAILS ON 17 OF 17 PAGES WALKED, and the fix is ADOPTION, not a new message
findings.detail: FAILURE STATES ARE INJECTED, never waited for. failures() intercepts the page's own reads and answers them with the failure under test, then reads what the page TELLS A PERSON. Every mutating verb is answered by a stub rather than forwarded - decided by blockWrite across the WHOLE Supabase surface, rpc and edge functions included - so nothing reaches the shared test database. The path is verified unchanged across the injection, and the surface is asserted before it: an expired session earlier today made 19 of 22 pages return identical landing-page readings, and 3 pages were REFUSED by that guard on this very sweep rather than measured. The navigation fence held on 16 of 16 pages read. THE ORACLE IS WHAT THE READER IS TOLD, not whether an error was caught. A caught error that renders nothing is indistinguishable, from the reader's side, from success. Stamped ::v=3: the top-level digest is a SET of per-statement content hashes, so a shared-library append expires nothing while a modify or delete correctly expires. Self-tested 8/8. FINDING: Injecting a 401 into this page's reads, the page does not tell the reader their session expired, does not name the session as the cause, and does not state the consequence for what they were doing. THE REFLEX IS TO WRITE THE MISSING MESSAGE AND THAT WOULD BE WRONG - it already exists. utils.js:1568 reads 'Your session expired, so nothing was saved. Sign in again and redo this step.' and :1611 has the read equivalent, with _WH_PG_DENIAL at :1518 and a careful 401-versus-403 note beneath it. There is even a comment recording that this was fixed once on the inquiry path, where a 42501 told a SIGNED-IN buyer their session had expired, and that 'the shared helper kept the bug for every other path'. Writing a new string would add a second source of truth for text that is already correct. SO THE DEFECT IS ADOPTION: the read path catches the status and never renders whReadError's text. A uniform 17-of-17 failure is not seventeen independent lapses, it is one shared path swallowing the status - which means ONE fix earns all seventeen rows in a single sweep. Same shape as the other platform-wide finds in this arc: ::placeholder absent everywhere, companion-launcher.js with no prefers-reduced-motion block at all. AND THE PROBE IS NOT AT FAULT, which matters before acting on a 17/17 result: fail_null_field passes on 16 of 16 pages under the same injection harness. A broken probe does not pass one injection everywhere and fail another everywhere. Row stays owed; measure adoption at the point of RENDER, not by the helper's existence.

evidence.asserts: when the session expires mid-read the page SAYS so - it states that something failed and names the session as the cause, rather than falling silent or offering a bare retry that cannot work
evidence.checked: FIXED BEFORE BANKED, AND THE DIAGNOSIS IS WHY THE FIX IS ONE EDIT INSTEAD OF 118. Injecting a 401 into each page's own reads and reading what the page then TELLS A PERSON failed on 12 of 12 pages measured, and the shape of the failures was the clue: 8 pages said NOTHING at all, 2 said 'failed' without naming the session, 2 named the session without saying anything failed, and not one of the twelve told the reader whether their work survived. Each speaking page supplied exactly ONE of the two halves a reader needs - which is what hand-rolled messages look like, not what a shared helper produces. AND THE HELPER ALREADY EXISTED AND ALREADY SAID BOTH HALVES: utils.js whReadError renders 'Your session expired, so <thing> could not be loaded', with _WH_PG_DENIAL and a careful 401-versus-403 note beside it, plus a comment recording that this was fixed once on the inquiry path where a 42501 told a SIGNED-IN buyer their session had expired, and that 'the shared helper kept the bug for every other path'. Writing a new string would have added a second source of truth for correct text. SO THE DEFECT WAS ADOPTION, MEASURED: 118 annotated `catch (_) { empty-catch-allow: best-effort silent swallow }` blocks across 11 pages, against exactly ONE page calling whReadError - public-feed, which is also the only page with ZERO silent swallows. That inverse correlation is the whole diagnosis: one architectural habit applied 118 times, each consciously annotated and passed review, not twelve oversights. 'Best-effort silent swallow' is a defensible posture for a tile that cannot compute; it is not defensible for the one read failure the reader must be told about. THE FIX GOES WHERE THE READS ALREADY PASS. Every client on this platform routes through getDb() - there is a registered gate asserting exactly that - and its _timeoutFetch wrapper already bounds every PostgREST/Auth/Storage request, its own comment noting that 'one install here covers all db.from()/db.rpc()/db.auth/db.storage calls platform-wide, so no page reinvents it'. A 401 seen there is now surfaced ONCE through the platform's own whToast/whBanner, debounced to one notice per 8s burst so parallel reads do not stack, with a self-declared role=status live region as the last resort. The 118 catch blocks are UNTOUCHED - a tile that cannot compute still fails quietly, the reader is simply now told the SESSION is why. 403 IS DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED. Under RLS a 403 is a PERMISSION answer to a LIVE session; only 401 means the session died. Answering both with 'sign in again' sends half the cases to fix the one thing that is not broken - the rule this file already states, and which hive currently breaks in the other direction by answering a 500 with session language. AND FINDING IT REQUIRED FIXING THE PROBE TWICE, both worth knowing. First, failures() had no interception guard: it re-fires loaders as window[k], so a page keeping them closure-scoped issues ZERO reads, the injection lands nowhere, and a false ok follows - indistinguishable from a page that swallowed the status. Every injected fetch now COUNTS what it intercepts, _reads travels with the result, and a verdict resting on zero reads is forced to null with vacuous:true rather than false. Second, and harder: the central notice RENDERED and was verifiably in the DOM, and fail_401 still read every sub-assertion false - because the probe's text scope was <main>, and a fixed-position notice must be a direct child of <body> (a fixed element inside a transformed or overflow-clipped ancestor positions against that ancestor, not the viewport). main.innerText could never contain it. Same shape as the contrast lens that once scoped to <main> while the report mounted outside and measured 15 of 518 nodes. The failure oracle now reads main PLUS live/alert/notice regions, deduped, and deliberately NOT all of body - nav and hub chrome carry standing words like 'offline' and 'retry' that would forge a pass on every page. Stamped ::v=3: the top-level digest is a SET of per-statement content hashes, so a shared-library append expires nothing while a modify or delete correctly expires. Self-tested 8/8. RESULT ON THIS PAGE: 6 of its own REST reads were intercepted and answered 401, so the injection genuinely landed (a verdict over 0 reads would be stamped vacuous and forced to null). saysExpiredOrFailed TRUE and namesSession TRUE. The notice reads 'Your session expired, so this page could not be loaded, and nothing you did was saved. Sign in again to continue.' VERIFIED ACROSS THE PLATFORM: 14 of 14 pages pass after this one edit, 0 still failing, 0 vacuous - which is the evidence that the fix is central rather than fourteen coincidences.

findings.title: RETRACTED - the fail_timeout failure I recorded here was MY main-scoped text read missing a body-level notice, not a defect on this page
findings.detail: RETRACTED - THIS WAS MY INSTRUMENT, NOT THIS PAGE. I recorded fail_timeout failing on 11 of 16 pages and fail_partial on 13 of 16, described them as pages that say nothing on a timeout and present a partial result as complete, and wrote per-page findings saying so. All four CC oracles now pass on 12 of 12 pages, and NOTHING was changed on any timeout or partial code path in between. What changed is the PROBE: its text scope was document.querySelector('main'), and these pages render their failure messages into toasts, banners and live regions - which are fixed-position and therefore direct children of <body>, because a fixed element inside a transformed or overflow-clipped ancestor positions against that ancestor instead of the viewport. main.innerText could never contain them. So the pages were speaking and the probe was deaf. HOW I FOUND IT, and why it is worth recording rather than quietly re-banking: I added a central 401 notice at getDb()'s transport seam, VERIFIED it rendering - the element was in the DOM carrying the text - and fail_401 still read every sub-assertion false. WHAT SURVIVES: the fail_401 finding was REAL. Before the central fix there was no session notice on any page at all - no element existed to be missed - so 12 of 12 pages genuinely told a reader nothing when their session died, and the fix at getDb() is what created the notice they now show. That one is not withdrawn. Only the timeout and partial claims are, and they are withdrawn in full. THE LESSON IS THE ONE THIS ARC KEEPS RE-LEARNING: an instrument that measures the wrong REGION produces well-formed readings, and a uniform failure across many pages should raise suspicion of the probe before it is written up as a platform defect. findings.detail: MEASURED with tools/prove_source_chip.mjs, live: 41 views graded across the roster - 18 make a TRUE provenance claim, 23 make NO claim, 0 name a feed they never read. THE ORACLE MATTERS MORE THAN MOST UI TEXT: a source chip is a promise that a number came from named feeds, and a reader uses it to decide whether to trust the figure. A chip naming a feed the page never queried is worse than no chip, because it manufactures confidence. SO THE CLAIM IS CHECKED AGAINST THE NETWORK, not the source: every PostgREST /rest/v1/<relation> the view actually requests is captured at runtime, and each schema-shaped token the chip names must correspond to one. It is deliberately ONE-DIRECTIONAL - a chip that SUMMARISES is fine, a chip that INVENTS is not. ★TWO MANUFACTURED FINDINGS WERE CAUGHT AND REMOVED BEFORE ANY OF THIS WAS BANKED. The first version of the token test counted the bare word `logbook`, so asset-hub and analytics were both reported as naming an unread feed - on the strength of ordinary prose: 'Based on your asset records, risk scores, logbook, failure analysis'. That is a sentence describing FEATURES to a person, not an assertion about a table, and analytics is right on its own terms - it reads analytics_snapshots, a snapshot DERIVED from logbook data, which is precisely what 'saved snapshot ... based on your logbook' says. A keyword match over human prose is how a page's own helper text becomes a defect. The test now counts a token only when it is unmistakably schema-shaped (a v_ prefix, a _truth suffix, or a known table prefix + underscore); bare English words never qualify. ★AND THE VIEW IS READ INSIDE ITSELF. V1 is graded at page scope and V2 inside the OPENED view via the shared tools/dialog_targets.mjs registry, because crediting a V2 row with a V1 reading is the one-measurement-swept-two-views error this bank has already paid for once. NOT BANKED GREEN: this view displays NO source chip at all (0 on screen while the surface requested 5 relation(s)). A surface that makes no provenance claim has not made a TRUE one, and the oracle asks whether the claim is true - so silence cannot satisfy it. Scoring it green would credit the absence of a promise as a kept promise. THIS IS ALSO NOT AUTOMATICALLY A DEFECT. Most of the 23 are V2 dialogs - a composer, a confirm sheet, a detail panel - which display a form rather than a derived figure, and a provenance chip on a surface that states no number would be noise. WHAT SETTLES IT is the per-view question the bank actually asks: does THIS view show a figure a reader would want provenance for? If yes, the chip is missing and this is a real finding; if no, the row is declared-na under R10 with 'this view states no derived figure' as the reason and the CM comprehension oracles as its replacement. Left owed rather than guessed, because that question is per-view and answering it from a count would be inventing the verdict.

Most numbers on this platform are COUNTS - 9 open jobs, 28 PMs overdue - and a count has no unit to show; flagging those would redden every surface, and a check that reddens everything is measuring itself. (1) It first accepted only BARE digits, so any value already carrying its unit never entered the set - 21 of 22 pages reported '0 judged' on a platform that renders MTBF and OEE nearly everywhere. An implausible abstention is an instrument fault, not a finding. (2) It then failed analytics on 'total downtime = 717.9h' because the time vocabulary listed hr/hrs/hours but not a bare 'h'. An oracle's vocabulary IS the oracle. Both are fixed and recorded in the tool. A raw COUNT explains itself - 'Open Jobs 9' is nine jobs. A PERCENTAGE, RATE, SCORE, INDEX or COMPOSITE is computed from things the reader cannot see, and that is where the meaning lives off-screen. evidence.asserts: the bulk condition this oracle names - enough rows to paginate - does not exist in this dataset, so there is no second page for a row to appear on twice
evidence.checked: Measured live, and TWO attempts to manufacture the condition failed for stated reasons rather than being abandoned. THE DATASET: the feed holds 15 public posts and the page requests limit=20, so a single request returns everything and the 'Load More' control correctly never appears - 'no more' is the right answer, not a pager bug. ATTEMPT 1, seed 50 rows: rejected, because writing 50 posts into the shared test database is exactly the pollution this bank forbids. ATTEMPT 2, shrink the page size: the request was intercepted and its limit rewritten from 20 to 4, leaving the data untouched so the page's own cursor logic would run across real boundaries. It rendered 4 cards and then reported 'no more' - because the page sets _hasMore by comparing the returned count against its OWN PAGE_SIZE constant, so a rewritten limit makes 4 === 20 false and hides the control. The probe defeats the mechanism it is trying to exercise; that is a limit of the instrument, not a defect in the page. WHAT IS PROVEN, and why this is not a hidden failure: the mechanism that would guarantee the oracle IS verified on the wire - the request goes out as 'order=created_at.desc,id.asc' with a UNIQUE tiebreaker on id, so equal created_at values have a defined relative order and a keyset cursor cannot skip or repeat across pages. What is unverified is only the multi-page TRAVERSAL, which needs 50 rows to exist. DECLARED-NA rather than PASS, because passing on a condition the data cannot produce is a green over an empty set. TO SETTLE IT LATER: seed a disposable hive with 50+ public posts via the seeders, or raise the fixture volume - then page through and compare the union against the source. Read-only: one limit rewrite in flight, no write issued.
evidence.value_checked: 15 public posts vs limit=20 (single request, no pager); wire query 'public=eq.true&flagged=eq.false&order=created_at.desc,id.asc&limit=20' - unique id tiebreaker present; limit rewritten to 4 rendered 4 cards, 4 distinct, 0 duplicates, then _hasMore false because 4 !== PAGE_SIZE

findings.title: NOT BANKED - THE PROBE COULD NOT TELL THE TWO POSTS APART, AND THE NEAR-MISS IS THE FINDING.
findings.detail: NOT BANKED - THE PROBE COULD NOT TELL THE TWO POSTS APART, AND THE NEAR-MISS IS THE FINDING. The anatomy names 'public <-> community (the same post on two surfaces)' as this page's cross-page seam, so the test is: a post marked public appears on BOTH surfaces, and a hive-only post appears ONLY on community. I drove it by matching a CONTENT SNIPPET on each surface. Both surfaces showed the text, and the 'hive-only' post appeared to render on the PUBLIC feed - which reads as a privacy leak, the single most serious defect this surface could have. ★IT IS NOT A LEAK. The seeded content is DUPLICATED across SIX posts with the same opening text: one public=true (085869d5) and five public=false (0f78265c, ed64b3ea, and three in other hives). public-feed was correctly rendering the PUBLIC copy; community was showing a hive-only copy; and my text match called them the same post. They never were. ★A CONTENT SNIPPET IS NOT AN IDENTITY. The post ids were available in the database and in the DOM the whole time - community renders each post in an element id'd 'post-<uuid>' - and I matched on text because it was the easier thing to see. On an oracle whose entire claim is 'the SAME object reads the same in two places', identity is the one thing that cannot be approximated. WHAT THIS WOULD HAVE COST: reporting that a hive-only post leaks to the public feed, on a platform where post visibility is stated BEFORE posting and is the thing a person cannot take back. A false privacy defect is not a harmless over-report - it would have sent someone to 'fix' a filter that is working correctly. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT, and it is small: match on the POST ID, not the text. Pick a known public id and assert it renders on both; pick a known hive-only id and assert it renders on community and NOT on public-feed. The counts already discriminate - 15 public platform-wide, 7 public in this hive, 24 hive posts total - so a mis-scoped read is visible in the numbers as well as the identity.

The anatomy names 'public <-> community (the same post on two surfaces)' as this seam. ★ATTEMPT 1 MATCHED A CONTENT SNIPPET AND NEARLY REPORTED A PRIVACY LEAK. Both surfaces showed the text, and the hive-only post appeared to render on the PUBLIC feed. findings.title: The DB's legible rate-limit message is likely MASKED by a generic client string on the write path
findings.detail: The refusal this row banks on is excellent AT ITS SOURCE: 'You have logged today's free limit (100). Resets at midnight.' with HINT logbook_daily_user. But the client does not necessarily show it. logbook.html:1885 renders save failures as a fixed string - 'Could not save. Check your connection and try again.' - which is not only generic but WRONG for this case: the connection is fine, the person hit a daily cap, and 'try again' is the one instruction guaranteed to fail until midnight. So the platform can produce a genuinely good limit message and still tell the reader to retry immediately. This is the mirror image of a defect fixed earlier in this same session, where pages echoed the RAW upstream message to the reader: the lesson is not 'always show the server string' nor 'never show it', but that a write path needs to distinguish a LIMIT (legible, actionable, has a reset time) from a FAULT (retry may work) - and the HINT key exists precisely so it can. NOT ESCALATED TO A FAILURE on this row because the oracle asks whether the rate limit is legible, and at the layer that produces it, it is - verifiably, with a machine-readable key. TO FINISH: on the write error path, branch on the hint/SQLSTATE (logbook_daily_user, 54000) and surface the server's own sentence plus its reset time instead of the connection string. Then re-walk this oracle at the client layer.

evidence.asserts: when a limit is hit the refusal is legible - it names the limit, the scope, and when it clears, and carries a machine-readable key so a client can tell WHICH limit fired
evidence.checked: FIRED FOR REAL, NOT READ FROM THE SOURCE - and then the source was read to confirm the second tier. Inside BEGIN ... ROLLBACK as an authenticated member (role SET, not just claims), a burst of 400 logbook inserts was attempted. The trigger refused with: **'You have logged today's free limit (100). Resets at midnight.'** carrying HINT 'logbook_daily_user'. Verified clean afterwards: 0 probe rows survived the rollback. WHY THIS COUNTS AS LEGIBLE, CLAUSE BY CLAUSE: it names the LIMIT (100), names WHAT was hit (today's free limit, i.e. a per-user daily cap rather than a system fault), tells the reader WHEN IT CLEARS ('Resets at midnight') so they know whether to wait or escalate, and ships a machine-readable HINT key ('logbook_daily_user') so a client can branch on WHICH limit fired instead of pattern-matching English. That combination - human sentence plus stable key - is what separates a legible limit from 'permission denied'. THERE IS A SECOND TIER AND IT IS ALSO LEGIBLE: check_hive_quota_logbook raises 'logbook cumulative quota exceeded for hive % (% >= %)' with ERRCODE 54000 and a HINT that old records can be archived - so the per-user daily cap and the per-hive cumulative quota are distinguishable by SQLSTATE and by message, and the hive-level one tells the reader the remedy (archive) rather than just the fact. ANCHORED ON supabase/migrations PER A13 - the message lives in the trigger body.

findings.title: auth_uid is bound from the JWT, but the display column worker_name is stored exactly as the body supplied it
findings.detail: MEASURED, in the same rolled-back probe that proves this row green. Writing as Hector (JWT sub 8fb252f7-...) while supplying auth_uid = Romeo's id AND worker_name = 'Romeo Beltran': the stored auth_uid was corrected to Hector's by trg_bind_submitter_logbook, and the stored worker_name remained 'Romeo Beltran'. So a row whose worker_name disagrees with its auth_uid is attributed to the WRONG PERSON in every list that reads it, while looking perfectly consistent to any check that only inspects auth_uid. logbook is the platform's evidence base: it feeds MTBF, PM compliance and a person's resume evidence, so misattribution is not cosmetic. NOT ESCALATED TO A FAILURE because the oracle asks whether identity comes from the JWT rather than the body, and for the identity column it does. TO FINISH: either derive worker_name from auth_uid in the same trigger that already binds auth_uid (it is one lookup away and the trigger is already there), or make the reads key on auth_uid so the display name cannot drive attribution. The first is the smaller change and keeps the existing read patterns working.

THESE ROWS WERE OWED ON A FALSE PREMISE, and that is worth recording because the premise was in our OWN TOOLING. Two provers documented that these oracles 'need the REST gateway, which is not reachable from this shell (kong publishes no host port)', and one copied that sentence into banked evidence. It was wrong: docker ps shows supabase_kong_workhive 0.0.0.0:54321->8000/tcp, and one curl with the publishable key answers 200. A ceiling written into a tool's docstring stops reading like a claim and starts reading like documentation, so it survived across sessions and kept ~130 rows owed. Corrected in place in both files rather than deleted. HOW IT WAS MEASURED: real HTTP GETs against the LIVE local gateway (http://127.0.0.1:54321/rest/v1), 40 relations, as three personas - anonymous with the publishable key, an AUTHENTICATED member (a real minted JWT for the seeded test identity), and a request carrying NO apikey at all. GET only, so nothing is written and there is nothing to roll back. Per relation: a collection read; the same read authenticated; the same read unauthenticated; a single-object read (Accept: application/vnd.pgrst.object+json) of a row that cannot exist; a read naming a column that does not exist; and a Prefer: count=exact read. AND THE PROBE'S OWN FIRST RUN REPORTED TWO DEFECTS THAT WERE BOTH MINE, corrected before anything was banked. It probed ?id=eq.<uuid> on every relation, but community_xp is keyed (worker_name, hive_id) and has no id column, so the request returned 42703 'column does not exist' - my malformed query read back as the gateway's misbehaviour. And it treated projects' 42501 'insufficient privilege' as a shape violation when a refusal carrying a machine-readable code is a CORRECT envelope - on this platform it is the better behaviour. A probe that assumes a schema it never checked produces findings about itself.

THESE ROWS WERE OWED ON A FALSE PREMISE, and that is worth recording because the premise was in our OWN TOOLING. Two provers documented that these oracles 'need the REST gateway, which is not reachable from this shell (kong publishes no host port)', and one copied that sentence into banked evidence. It was wrong: docker ps shows supabase_kong_workhive 0.0.0.0:54321->8000/tcp, and one curl with the publishable key answers 200. A ceiling written into a tool's docstring stops reading like a claim and starts reading like documentation, so it survived across sessions and kept ~130 rows owed. Corrected in place in both files rather than deleted. HOW IT WAS MEASURED: real HTTP GETs against the LIVE local gateway (http://127.0.0.1:54321/rest/v1), 40 relations, as three personas - anonymous with the publishable key, an AUTHENTICATED member (a real minted JWT for the seeded test identity), and a request carrying NO apikey at all. GET only, so nothing is written and there is nothing to roll back. Per relation: a collection read; the same read authenticated; the same read unauthenticated; a single-object read (Accept: application/vnd.pgrst.object+json) of a row that cannot exist; a read naming a column that does not exist; and a Prefer: count=exact read. scenarios.oracle: the component's loading state is distinguishable from its empty state

evidence.asserts: the component reaches a settled, populated state - no node is left in a permanent loading or skeleton shimmer, and the states the page announces during load (skeleton, aria-busy, disabled) are the ones it actually uses
evidence.checked: 2026-08-20 gate:ck_component_states - clean full run: 22 pages, controlFailed [] and stuck [], measured with a MutationObserver armed from the FIRST MUTATION rather than after settle
evidence.value_checked:
0 stuck of 22 pages, and the detector is proven live on EVERY page rather than by a separate mode: the prover APPENDS a real skeleton node (class 'skeleton wh-control-probe') and asserts the observer count ROSE (controlCaught: after > before), enforcing it under --gate via results.filter(r => r.controlCaught !== true). So a page reporting 0 skeletons has PROVEN it can see one. Measuring after settle is how 'this page has no loading state' gets recorded for a page that paints nine skeleton rows during load - hive did exactly that, and a candidate now counts as a skeleton only at placeholder GEOMETRY (>=24px both axes, or an explicit skeleton/shimmer class), because an 8px dot is a status light and a 648x260 block is a skeleton
 | depends_on: tools/prove_component_states.mjs

findings.title: NOT BANKED, BECAUSE THE PASS IS VACUOUS ON THIS VIEW - and the prover's own numbers are what show it.
findings.detail: NOT BANKED, BECAUSE THE PASS IS VACUOUS ON THIS VIEW - and the prover's own numbers are what show it. tools/prove_dialog_a11y.mjs graded 36 of 43 registry targets with ZERO failing, and its summary line reads 'every focusable control shows a causally-verified focus indicator'. On this view that sentence is true the way any statement about an empty set is true: the report records focus.candidates = 0 and focus.checked = 0. No focusable control was examined, so nothing about focus indication was established. Banking it green would put a row in the bank whose evidence is an empty denominator - the exact false green this bank exists to prevent. THIS IS A PROPERTY OF THE VIEW, NOT A DEFECT. Six of the thirty-six graded views hold no focusable controls at all - engineering-design's guide tab, shift-brain's verdict summary and its details disclosure, report-sender's contacts list, public-feed's feed list, achievements' recent list. They are READ surfaces: text, cards and figures. A view with nothing to focus cannot fail a focus oracle, and it cannot pass one either. WORTH SEPARATING FROM THE SIBLING ORACLES, because they are NOT vacuous here: this same run measured accessible names and reduced-motion on the same views and those are real readings - a name applies to any control, focusable or not, and 'nothing animates under prefers-reduced-motion' is a statement about the whole subtree. So the a11y run is only empty for FOCUS on these six. WHAT WOULD SETTLE THIS ROW: either the view genuinely gains an interactive control (then re-run and grade it), or the row is dispositioned declared-na with this reason under R10 - which needs a replacement oracle named, and the honest replacement is that the view is READABLE and its figures are labelled (CL contrast + CM what_is_this_number), not that its focus ring works. AND AN INSTRUMENT NOTE, since the prover is otherwise strong: its per-view PASS does not distinguish 'checked N controls, all good' from 'checked none'. The distinction is recoverable only from focus.candidates in the report, so a consumer that reads the exit code alone would bank all six of these as proven. The count belongs in the printed line.

observed.verdict: vacuous - no focusable control exists on this view, so the oracle is neither passed nor failed
observed.siblings_are_real: accessible-name and reduced-motion readings on this same view are NOT vacuous
observed.views_in_this_class: 6 of 36 graded - engineering-design V3, shift-brain V2 + V3, report-sender V2, public-feed V3, achievements V2
observed.instrument_note: the printed PASS does not distinguish 'checked N, all good' from 'checked none'; only focus.candidates reveals it
observed.to_settle: gain a real interactive control and re-run, or disposition declared-na with a replacement oracle (readability + labelled figures)

evidence.checked: PASSES: reached value: 2438 chars, 6 actionable control(s), 0 stuck skeletons, 0 failed read(s). PERSONA: this row was walked as "anon (the primary reader)" (slot P1), the label this page's own anatomy names, established as identity 'anon'. HOW THE JOURNEY WAS CONSTRUCTED. Each row is walked live in a throwaway browser context as the persona the page's OWN anatomy names: page_bank_anatomy/<page>.json `journey_personas` supplies the label (e.g. 'worker (own entries)', 'two_context (two techs, one PM)'), and the harness maps it to an identity it can actually establish - supervisor and worker are real signed-in accounts, anon and crawler get no session, two_context opens BOTH accounts concurrently on the same page. A label that maps to no identity is FAILED, never defaulted to a signed-in worker and never skipped: defaulting is exactly how a persona claim gets banked for the wrong identity. FIRST RUN means everything a returning visitor would CARRY is removed, while everything that constitutes their IDENTITY is preserved: localStorage and sessionStorage are cleared apart from the sb-*/supabase auth keys, the hive-membership keys (wh_active_hive_id / wh_hive_id / wh_hive_role / wh_hive_name) and the worker-name keys (wh_last_worker / wh_worker_name / workerName). Wiping auth would test the sign-in wall instead of the journey; wiping the other two would test a DIFFERENT person entirely. evidence.asserts: a link that leaves this surface carries its context with it, and the receiving surface arrives in the state that context names rather than its default
evidence.checked: A live two-surface walk with a control. ORIGIN: this page links to 'marketplace.html?section=services' (public-feed). THE CONTROL IS WHAT MAKES THIS NON-VACUOUS: loaded WITHOUT the parameter the destination shows Parts active and Services inactive - Parts is the default - while WITH '?section=services' Parts goes inactive and Services becomes active. So the two arrivals are distinguishable states and the difference is exactly the context handed over. Read-only: page loads only, nothing written; each identity used a fully separate browser context so none could inherit another's session or cache.

findings.detail: MEASURED with tools/prove_journey.mjs --journeys j5, walked live: 16 composer(s) across the roster, ZERO failing. THE JOURNEY: type into a composer, get called away, come back - and nothing may have half-landed. It is the most ordinary thing that happens to someone on a plant floor, and the failure it hunts is a page that treats abandoned input as a committed record. ★THE DISCRIMINATION THAT MAKES THE VERDICT FAIR, and without which this oracle would punish good behaviour: after the reload the marker text is looked for in TWO places, and they mean opposite things. Back inside the COMPOSER FIELD means a DRAFT was deliberately preserved - that is good UX and passes. Out in the page's own CONTENT means it half-landed, and a person who typed and walked away now owns a record they never submitted - that fails. A checker that merely searched the page for the text would call the good case and the bad case the same thing. NON-WRITING BY CONSTRUCTION: nothing is ever submitted; the marker only ever reaches an input's value, so this prover cannot pollute the shared test database. The composer inventory comes from tools/dialog_targets.mjs - the same grounded registry four other provers read - so which views count as composers cannot drift from how those views are known to open.FOR THIS PAGE AND PERSONA THERE IS NOTHING TO ABANDON. The prover walked all 66 (page, persona) pairs and reached a composer on 16 of them; this pair reported no composer at all, so the journey could not be CONSTRUCTED. ★THAT IS RECORDED AS UNBUILT, NOT AS A PASS, and the distinction is the whole point: a journey that cannot be constructed must never be scored green, because 'nothing half-landed' is trivially true of a surface where nothing can be typed. The prover carries that rail explicitly - non-vacuity, a journey that cannot be built is a finding rather than a quiet skip - and banking it green would be the empty-denominator failure this bank exists to catch. WHY THIS PAIR HAS NONE: the composer inventory is tools/dialog_targets.mjs, and a composer is only counted when it is reachable FOR THIS IDENTITY. index's fields, for instance, live on the anon landing and the sign-in modal, so a signed-in persona has no composer on that page even though the page plainly contains inputs. A read-only surface (public-feed, achievements, the report pages) has none for any persona. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: either this pair genuinely has a composer the registry does not yet list - in which case the registry gains an entry and the prover reaches it - or the row is dispositioned declared-na under R10 with 'this surface has nothing to abandon' as the reason and the page's own CO recovery oracles as the replacement. Left owed rather than declared here, because deciding which of those two it is needs the per-page composer question answered, not assumed.

evidence.asserts: abandoning midway and returning leaves no half-applied state
evidence.checked: DECLARED-NA WITH A NAMED REPLACEMENT (rail R10), AND THE REASON IS THE ORACLE'S OWN WORD: MIDWAY. This oracle asks what happens when someone abandons PART-WAY THROUGH. On this page the person-caused action is nothing - it has no .insert/.update/.delete, no .rpc and no functions.invoke - there is no part-way. You either pressed it or you did not, so there is no half-applied state to leave behind and no draft to return to. ★WHY THIS IS RECORDED RATHER THAN PASSED: 'no half-applied state' over an action with no middle is VACUOUSLY TRUE, and a vacuous truth banked as a live-walk PASS is how coverage improves by deleting obligations. Fourteen OTHER surfaces on this platform DO have a midway - a capture modal, a composer, a multi-field form - and all fourteen were driven, filled and abandoned by reload. This page is not one of them, and the emptiness is the finding. ★THE REPLACEMENT, so the surface is not simply excused: what this page owes instead is that the effect its one press DOES cause is observable to the person who caused it - carried by effect_visible, already proven green here (PB-public-feed-072-CF-ufai-F-V1-effect_visible). A one-press surface is still accountable; it is accountable for a different sentence. ★AND ONE PAGE WAS DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED FROM THIS DISPOSITION: skillmatrix has no green effect_visible, because its exam could not be reached (SKILL_CONTENT is module-scoped and no discipline/level pair produced questions). Declaring NA there would excuse an obligation against a replacement that does not exist, which is the same vacuity wearing R10's clothes. Its rows stay owed with that diagnosis.

findings.detail: MEASURED with tools/prove_journey.mjs --journeys j5, walked live: 16 composer(s) across the roster, ZERO failing. THE JOURNEY: type into a composer, get called away, come back - and nothing may have half-landed. It is the most ordinary thing that happens to someone on a plant floor, and the failure it hunts is a page that treats abandoned input as a committed record. ★THE DISCRIMINATION THAT MAKES THE VERDICT FAIR, and without which this oracle would punish good behaviour: after the reload the marker text is looked for in TWO places, and they mean opposite things. Back inside the COMPOSER FIELD means a DRAFT was deliberately preserved - that is good UX and passes. Out in the page's own CONTENT means it half-landed, and a person who typed and walked away now owns a record they never submitted - that fails. A checker that merely searched the page for the text would call the good case and the bad case the same thing. NON-WRITING BY CONSTRUCTION: nothing is ever submitted; the marker only ever reaches an input's value, so this prover cannot pollute the shared test database. The composer inventory comes from tools/dialog_targets.mjs - the same grounded registry four other provers read - so which views count as composers cannot drift from how those views are known to open.FOR THIS PAGE AND PERSONA THERE IS NOTHING TO ABANDON. The prover walked all 66 (page, persona) pairs and reached a composer on 16 of them; this pair reported no composer at all, so the journey could not be CONSTRUCTED. ★THAT IS RECORDED AS UNBUILT, NOT AS A PASS, and the distinction is the whole point: a journey that cannot be constructed must never be scored green, because 'nothing half-landed' is trivially true of a surface where nothing can be typed. The prover carries that rail explicitly - non-vacuity, a journey that cannot be built is a finding rather than a quiet skip - and banking it green would be the empty-denominator failure this bank exists to catch. WHY THIS PAIR HAS NONE: the composer inventory is tools/dialog_targets.mjs, and a composer is only counted when it is reachable FOR THIS IDENTITY. index's fields, for instance, live on the anon landing and the sign-in modal, so a signed-in persona has no composer on that page even though the page plainly contains inputs. A read-only surface (public-feed, achievements, the report pages) has none for any persona. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: either this pair genuinely has a composer the registry does not yet list - in which case the registry gains an entry and the prover reaches it - or the row is dispositioned declared-na under R10 with 'this surface has nothing to abandon' as the reason and the page's own CO recovery oracles as the replacement. Left owed rather than declared here, because deciding which of those two it is needs the per-page composer question answered, not assumed.

On this page the person-caused action is nothing - it has no .insert/.update/.delete, no .rpc and no functions.invoke - there is no part-way. You either pressed it or you did not, so there is no half-applied state to leave behind and no draft to return to. ★WHY THIS IS RECORDED RATHER THAN PASSED: 'no half-applied state' over an action with no middle is VACUOUSLY TRUE, and a vacuous truth banked as a live-walk PASS is how coverage improves by deleting obligations. Fourteen OTHER surfaces on this platform DO have a midway - a capture modal, a composer, a multi-field form - and all fourteen were driven, filled and abandoned by reload. This page is not one of them, and the emptiness is the finding. ★THE REPLACEMENT, so the surface is not simply excused: what this page owes instead is that the effect its one press DOES cause is observable to the person who caused it - carried by effect_visible, already proven green here (PB-public-feed-072-CF-ufai-F-V1-effect_visible). A one-press surface is still accountable; it is accountable for a different sentence. ★AND ONE PAGE WAS DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED FROM THIS DISPOSITION: skillmatrix has no green effect_visible, because its exam could not be reached (SKILL_CONTENT is module-scoped and no discipline/level pair produced questions). Declaring NA there would excuse an obligation against a replacement that does not exist, which is the same vacuity wearing R10's clothes. Its rows stay owed with that diagnosis.

findings.title: MEASURED with tools/prove_journey.mjs --journeys j5, walked live: 16 composer(s) across the roster, ZERO failing.
findings.detail: MEASURED with tools/prove_journey.mjs --journeys j5, walked live: 16 composer(s) across the roster, ZERO failing. THE JOURNEY: type into a composer, get called away, come back - and nothing may have half-landed. It is the most ordinary thing that happens to someone on a plant floor, and the failure it hunts is a page that treats abandoned input as a committed record. ★THE DISCRIMINATION THAT MAKES THE VERDICT FAIR, and without which this oracle would punish good behaviour: after the reload the marker text is looked for in TWO places, and they mean opposite things. Back inside the COMPOSER FIELD means a DRAFT was deliberately preserved - that is good UX and passes. Out in the page's own CONTENT means it half-landed, and a person who typed and walked away now owns a record they never submitted - that fails. A checker that merely searched the page for the text would call the good case and the bad case the same thing. NON-WRITING BY CONSTRUCTION: nothing is ever submitted; the marker only ever reaches an input's value, so this prover cannot pollute the shared test database. The composer inventory comes from tools/dialog_targets.mjs - the same grounded registry four other provers read - so which views count as composers cannot drift from how those views are known to open.FOR THIS PAGE AND PERSONA THERE IS NOTHING TO ABANDON. The prover walked all 66 (page, persona) pairs and reached a composer on 16 of them; this pair reported no composer at all, so the journey could not be CONSTRUCTED. ★THAT IS RECORDED AS UNBUILT, NOT AS A PASS, and the distinction is the whole point: a journey that cannot be constructed must never be scored green, because 'nothing half-landed' is trivially true of a surface where nothing can be typed. The prover carries that rail explicitly - non-vacuity, a journey that cannot be built is a finding rather than a quiet skip - and banking it green would be the empty-denominator failure this bank exists to catch. WHY THIS PAIR HAS NONE: the composer inventory is tools/dialog_targets.mjs, and a composer is only counted when it is reachable FOR THIS IDENTITY. index's fields, for instance, live on the anon landing and the sign-in modal, so a signed-in persona has no composer on that page even though the page plainly contains inputs. A read-only surface (public-feed, achievements, the report pages) has none for any persona. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: either this pair genuinely has a composer the registry does not yet list - in which case the registry gains an entry and the prover reaches it - or the row is dispositioned declared-na under R10 with 'this surface has nothing to abandon' as the reason and the page's own CO recovery oracles as the replacement. Left owed rather than declared here, because deciding which of those two it is needs the per-page composer question answered, not assumed.

On this page the person-caused action is nothing - it has no .insert/.update/.delete, no .rpc and no functions.invoke - there is no part-way. You either pressed it or you did not, so there is no half-applied state to leave behind and no draft to return to. ★WHY THIS IS RECORDED RATHER THAN PASSED: 'no half-applied state' over an action with no middle is VACUOUSLY TRUE, and a vacuous truth banked as a live-walk PASS is how coverage improves by deleting obligations. Fourteen OTHER surfaces on this platform DO have a midway - a capture modal, a composer, a multi-field form - and all fourteen were driven, filled and abandoned by reload. This page is not one of them, and the emptiness is the finding. ★THE REPLACEMENT, so the surface is not simply excused: what this page owes instead is that the effect its one press DOES cause is observable to the person who caused it - carried by effect_visible, already proven green here (PB-public-feed-072-CF-ufai-F-V1-effect_visible). A one-press surface is still accountable; it is accountable for a different sentence. ★AND ONE PAGE WAS DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED FROM THIS DISPOSITION: skillmatrix has no green effect_visible, because its exam could not be reached (SKILL_CONTENT is module-scoped and no discipline/level pair produced questions). Declaring NA there would excuse an obligation against a replacement that does not exist, which is the same vacuity wearing R10's clothes. Its rows stay owed with that diagnosis.
